memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Bring the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him. They are to perform duties for him and for the whole community at the tent of meeting by doing the work of the tabernacle. They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, fulfilling the obligations of the Israelites by doing the work of the tabernacle." - Num 3:5-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tribe of Levi was given a clear role: to assist Aaron and to care for the tabernacle. They were the helpers, the ones who did the practical work that kept the worship of God going. Not every Levite stood at the altar as a priest, but every Levite had meaningful work to do.

There is great dignity in being a helper. Our world tends to celebrate the person out front, the leader, the one in charge. But God's work has always depended just as much on those who quietly serve behind the scenes — carrying, cleaning, caring, preparing.

The Levites' service made the worship of the whole community possible. Without them, the tabernacle could not function. Their "ordinary" work was actually sacred work, because it was done for God.

The same is true today. The person who sets up chairs, cooks the meal, cares for children, keeps things running — all of this is holy service when done for the Lord. The New Testament reminds us that whatever we do, we can do it as working for the Lord and not merely for people (Col 3:23-24).

Do not despise the role of a helper. In God's eyes, faithful helping is a high calling.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you value the "behind the scenes" service you offer?
- How can you serve God through practical, everyday help?
- Whose quiet service can you thank and encourage today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that even quiet, practical service is precious to You. Help me to serve faithfully, doing my work as unto You. Amen.
